name: Arduino UNO Q
identification: UNO-shaped board with two rows of black female pin headers along the long edges, a USB-C connector, an 8x13 LED matrix in the middle of the top side, and 'UNO Q' printed on it. The classic Arduino UNO R3/R4 looks similar but has a USB-B or different USB-C layout and no LED matrix: that is NOT this board.

facts.statement: The microcontroller is an STM32U585. It handles the 3.3 V headers JDIGITAL and JANALOG.
facts.source: Arduino UNO Q datasheet (SKU ABX00162-ABX00173), section 'Microcontroller'

facts.statement: All JDIGITAL lines (D0-D13) are 3.3 V logic. Most use an FT-type I/O structure and are 5 V-tolerant as inputs.
facts.source: Arduino UNO Q datasheet, section 9.6 'JDIGITAL - Pin Map'

facts.statement: D3 (PB0) is only 3.6 V-tolerant. Never apply 5 V to it in any mode.
facts.source: Arduino UNO Q datasheet, section 9.6 'JDIGITAL - Pin Map'

facts.statement: A0-A5 are not 5 V-tolerant in analog mode. Valid range is 0 V to VREF+ (about 3.3 V); the absolute maximum is VDD + 0.3 V, about 3.6 V.
facts.source: Arduino UNO Q datasheet, sections 9 'Peripherals' and 9.7 'JANALOG - Pin Map'

facts.statement: The +3V3 pin on the JANALOG header outputs the 3.3 V system rail (3.1 V min, 3.3 V typical, 3.5 V max).
facts.source: Arduino UNO Q datasheet, sections 3.2 'Recommended Operating Conditions' and 9.7

facts.statement: The JANALOG header carries +3V3, +5V (5V_SYS, 4.5-5.5 V from USB-C) and two GND pins.
facts.source: Arduino UNO Q datasheet, sections 3.1 'Input Power' and 9.7

facts.statement: The MCU-controlled RGB LEDs (LED3 on PH10-PH12, LED4 on PH13-PH15) are active-low: they turn on when driven to logic 0.
In the official Arduino core, the first built-in LED (LED_BUILTIN) is PH10, which is LED3 red. A forum thread reports it not blinking under IDE 2.3.7, so flash a blink sketch once before the demo.

With the official core arduino:zephyr 1.1.0 installed, `arduino-cli board listall` lists 'Arduino UNO Q' as arduino:zephyr:unoq. A sketch for it compiles with the arm-zephyr-eabi toolchain, not avr-gcc.
facts.source: arduino:zephyr 1.1.0 boards.txt, checked with arduino-cli 1.2.0 on 2026-11-14

facts.statement: Text output from a sketch reaches the computer through the Monitor object of the official Arduino_RouterBridge library (Monitor.begin(), Monitor.println()). It is routed through the board's Linux side.
Serial is the MCU's hardware UART on header pins D0/D1. It does not show up in the App Lab or IDE console.
Sketches are uploaded with the core's 'remoteocd' tool through the board's Linux side, not through a serial bootloader as on the classic UNO.
The board has an 8 x 13 blue LED matrix (104 LEDs) driven by the microcontroller. It shows the boot logo for about 20-30 seconds while Linux starts.

The matrix is driven with the Arduino_LED_Matrix library that ships with the core: declare `Arduino_LED_Matrix matrix;`, call `matrix.begin();` and `matrix.setGrayscaleBits(3);` in setup(), then `matrix.draw(frame);` where frame is a `uint8_t[104]`, row by row (8 rows of 13), each value 0 (off) to 7 (brightest).
